mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods when this trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals contraction in economic output, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines by more than 0.5% for four months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary pressure regime, which increases uncertainty and risk premia, driving negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages simultaneously.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 1,200,000 units for six consecutive months signals a deepening housing market downturn, which negatively impacts construction-related equities and consumer confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when HOUST remains below 1,200,000 for six months.

mechanism_narrative: A positive year-over-year change in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) exceeding 200,000 for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS YoY change > 200,000 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS grows by more than 200,000 per month for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% month-over-month simultaneously signals a broad-based demand collapse, which sharply reduces corporate revenue and equity valuations, producing large negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall > -1% MoM
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline by more than 1% month-over-month simultaneously.
